blocks.en: Deep generative networks have recently achieved unprecedented performance in precise image and video editing using sophisticated textual prompts. However, the effectiveness of such models heavily depends on access to very large supervised and annotated image datasets, which can be very difficult to obtain. This is particularly true for satellite instruments, which very rarely overlap with labelled data, and suffer from domain shifts in the rare occasions they do. In this paper, we investigate the potential of flow matching models for unsupervised domain adaptation of satellite radiometer images. Our main contribution is a novel unsupervised method that achieves precise domain alignment by leveraging parts of the deterministic ordinary differential equations in flow matching models, conditioned on different satellite instruments. A key strength of our approach is its ability to preserve essential information while adapting across any domains since the perturbations are in theory bijective. Extensive experiments conducted on the GPM-Core constellation show the benefit of our conditional domain adaptation, particularly in improving rain precipitation estimation from radiometer imagery.
blocks.zh: 深层基因网络最近利用精密的文字提示在精确图像和视频编辑上取得了前所未有的表现. 然而,这种模型的效能在很大程度上取决于能否取用非常庞大的有监督和附加说明的图像数据集,而这种数据集可能很难取用. 对于卫星仪器来说尤其如此,卫星仪器很少与标有标签的数据相重叠,并且很少发生域位变化。 在本文中,我们调查了流动匹配模型对卫星辐射计图像进行无监督域改造的潜力. 我们的主要贡献是一种新的不受监督的方法,它通过利用流量匹配模型中确定性普通微分方程的部分内容,以不同的卫星仪器为条件,实现精确的域调和. 我们方法的一个关键优势是,它有能力保存基本信息,同时在任何领域进行调整,因为扰动在理论上都是双向的。 在GPM-Core星座上进行的广泛实验表明,我们有条件的域适应的好处,特别是在通过辐射计图像改进降雨量估计方面。

blocks.en: Precipitation estimation from satellite imagery holds tremendous potential for both scientific and societal applications, as vast amounts of data are continuously acquired worldwide. Moreover, unlike ground-based radar observations — which are often sparse or entirely absent in many developing countries — satellite constellations provide near–real-time, global-scale coverage of the Earth’s surface. This capability is crucial not only for improving water resource management, but also for strengthening our ability to predict extreme hydrological events, such as major floods. This is particularly true for the Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) mission [ 17 ] , an international collaboration that provides unprecedented spatiotemporal coverage of global precipitation through a constellation of twelve satellites, primarily equipped with passive microwave radiometers. Within this constellation, the GPM Core Observatory (GPM-Core) plays a vital role, as it uniquely carries a dual-frequency precipitation radar (DPR) capable of directly estimating raining rates (RR), alongside the GPM Microwave Imager (GMI), which measures brightness temperatures (TB). This contrasts with the other satellites in the constellation, which are equipped only with passive microwave radiometers, and can measure only brightness temperatures. This unique feature of the GPM-Core satellite opens up promising opportunities for deep learning approaches that exploit the combined DPR and GMI measurements to enhance precipitation estimation. This is particularly true for the methods [ 21 , 15 ] , employing deep neural networks to predict rain rates using the GPM-Core satellite brightness temperatures, and which have shown the capability to outperform classical approaches like GPROF [ 11 ] . Among these methods, the strength of DRAIN [ 21 ] lies in its convolutional architecture, which exploits the spatial structure of 2D images rather than relying on independent per-pixel estimates as in GPROF — and consequently it often achieves superior performance. This approach is particularly compelling given that the swath of the DPR measurements on the GPM-Core satellite is nearly four times narrower than that of the GMI, enabling rain rate estimation over much larger spatial domains. However, despite those very impressive performances, the DRAIN algorithm does not generalize to other satellites from the constellation and achieves much poorer results when using the corresponding brightness temperatures. This is generally explained by the different orbit characteristics of the employed instruments such as channels, angle of view, or pixel resolutions. Although GPM-Core shares overlapping orbits with those other satellites, training a supervised domain-transfer algorithm is challenging, as these very scarce overlaps occur almost exclusively near 60 ∘ 60^{\circ} latitude north and south, making the model prone to geographical biases. Additionally, varying temporal offsets of up to 15 minutes exist between acquisitions, making those observations suitable only as pseudo ground truths. To tackle this challenge of non-colocated data in satellite imagery, more general strategies often turn to unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA), which has the key advantage of not requiring corresponding ground truth images. These approaches aim to transform the content of an image to match a target distribution by leveraging deep generative neural networks. Traditionally, such methods have heavily relied on Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) [ 6 , 9 ] , and in particular CycleGAN [ 22 ] , which allows for indirect supervision through a cycle-consistency reconstruction loss. This is the case for the methods in [ 16 ] , which use CycleGANs along with the DRAIN [ 21 ] to predict raining rates from the DMSP-F18 satellite of the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program. More precisely the images obtained with its SSMI/S microwave imager are modified so as to very closely match the distribution of those from GMI. Then, the DRAIN algorithm is run on those adapted images to obtain raining rates. By doing so, very promising results are obtained in [ 16 ] , and ultimately, the only drawback of the method is the notoriously unstable training of GANs [ 6 ] — which makes it very challenging for this method to be extended to other satellites from the constantly evolving GPM constellation. In order to address these aforementioned issues, we present a novel unsupervised domain adaptation method, based on the modern Flow Matching [ 12 , 1 , 20 ] paradigm so as to adapt brightness temperatures from the F18 satellite to those of the GPM instrument. The main advantage of this approach resides in the bijective nature of flow based models, which possess the remarkable ability of ”ideally” noising and denoising an image while preserving the most salient physical and structural information of the original image. Extensive experiments showcase the benefits of our approach, matching or outperforming other state-of-the-art approaches while being much easier to train.
blocks.zh: 卫星图像的降水估计对科学和社会应用都具有巨大潜力,因为世界各地不断获得大量数据。 此外,与地面雷达观测不同的是,卫星星座对地表的覆盖几乎是实时的,而地面雷达观测在许多发展中国家往往很少或完全不存在。 这种能力不仅对改进水资源管理,而且对加强我们预测诸如重大洪水等极端水文事件的能力至关重要。 全球降水测量任务[17]尤其如此,该国际合作通过12个卫星星座,主要是配备被动微波辐射计,对全球降水进行前所未有的瞬间覆盖。 在这个星座内,GPM核心观测台(GPM-Core)发挥着至关重要的作用,因为它独有地搭载了能直接估计出降雨速率的双频降水雷达(DPR),并配有测量亮度温度的GPM微波成像仪(GMI). 这与星座上的其他卫星形成对比,这些卫星只配备了被动微波辐射计,只能测量亮度温度. GPM-Core卫星的这一独特性为采用深层学习方法,利用DPR和GMI的综合测量方法来提高降水量估计提供了有希望的机会。 对于方法[21,15]来说尤其如此,它利用深层神经网络利用GPM-Core卫星亮度温度来预测降雨率,这些方法表明有能力超越GPROF等经典方法[11]. 在这些方法中, DRAIN [21] 的优点在于它的旋律结构,它利用了2D图像的空间结构,而不是像GPROF那样依赖独立的每像素估计——因此它常常达到优异的性能. 这种方法尤其具有说服力,因为GPM-Core卫星上的降雨率测量比GMI小近4倍,因此能够对更大的空间领域进行降雨率估计。 然而,尽管有这些令人印象深刻的表现,但DRAIN算法并没有向星座上的其他卫星概括,在使用相应的亮度温度时取得了更差的结果. 这一般由所使用仪器的不同轨道特征来解释,如通道,视角,或像素分辨率等. 虽然GPM-Core与其他卫星共用重叠轨道,但培训一个有监督的域-传输算法具有挑战性,因为这些极少数的重叠几乎完全发生在北纬和南纬60°C附近,使模型容易出现地理偏见。 此外,在收购之间存在着长达15分钟的不同时间抵消,使这些观察仅适合作为伪地事实。 为了应对卫星图像中非同地位数据的这一挑战,更一般的战略往往转向无监督域的适应(UDA),其关键优势是不需要相应的地面真象. 这些方法旨在通过利用深源神经网络来改变图像的内容,以匹配目标分布. 传统上,这种方法在很大程度上依赖于基因对抗网络(GANs)[6,9],特别是循环GAN[22],它允许通过周期一致性重建损失进行间接监督. [16]中的方法就是如此,这些方法使用CycleGANs和 DRAIN [21] 预测国防气象卫星方案的DMSP-F18卫星的降雨率。 更确切地说,用其SSMI/S微波成像仪获得的图像经过了修改,以便与GMI的图像分布非常相匹配。 然后,DRAIN算法运行在这些被改造的图像上,以获得降雨率. 通过这样做,在[16]中取得了非常有希望的结果,最终,该方法的唯一缺点是GANs[6]的出名的不稳定训练——这使得将这种方法推广到不断演变的GPM星座上的其他卫星非常有挑战性. 为了解决上述问题,我们介绍了一种新型的无监督域适应方法,其取自现代流相匹配[12, 1, 20]范式,使从F18卫星到GPM仪器的亮度温度相适应. 这种方法的主要优点在于流线模型具有双射性,这些模型在保存原始图像最显著的物理和结构信息的同时,具有“理想地”取名和去名的显著能力。 广泛的实验展示了我们的方法的好处,匹配或优于其他最先进的方法,同时容易训练。

blocks.en:
Deep generative models have widely been explored for unsupervised domain adaptation. Among them, GAN-based approaches [ 6 ] , particularly CycleGAN [ 22 ] and related image-to-image translation methods [ 9 ] , have historically achieved strong results. However their main drawback is the training instability and lack of diversity frequently observed with adversarial training objectives [ 6 ] . More recently, with the emergence of diffusion models [ 8 , 18 ] , novel interesting approaches have emerged as very competitive alternatives. Those include approaches like Flow Matching [ 12 , 1 , 20 ] , which are inspired by continuous normalizing flows [ 2 ] and retain the bijective properties inherited from normalizing flows [ 5 ] , while enabling simulation-free training and significantly faster sampling. Within this line of work, some very recent approaches go beyond the standard Gaussian assumption by allowing arbitrary source and target distributions [ 20 , 4 , 3 ] , thereby enabling the learning of a pushforward mapping directly between different image distributions. Recent related works also investigate unsupervised domain alignment through structured latent decompositions with the flow matching objective [ 10 ] . Alternatively, some works exploit the bijective nature of neural networks for unsupervised domain adaptation, most notably [ 7 ] employs normalizing flows with adversarial losses, and [ 19 ] reverses ordinary differential equations (ODEs) for diffusion models. The work in [ 19 ] is closely related to our approach but differs in three key aspects: (i) it trains a separate model for each modality rather than relying on conditional generative models; (ii) it integrates the entire ODE solver to map images fully to Gaussian noise, whereas we integrate only a portion of the trajectory to optimally add noise while preserving image content, and this also differs from stochastic partial noising strategies such as [ 13 ] ; and (iii) it adopts diffusion instead of the more recent flow-matching paradigm, which is known to yield straighter trajectories, faster integration, and improved image quality [ 12 ] .
Building on these advantages, we explore conditional flow-matching–based generative models as an alternative for unsupervised domain adaptation, motivated by their stable training, invertible bijective mappings, and well-defined likelihoods. Although this study considers a limited set of satellites, these properties make them promising for an extension to additional sensors in the GPM constellation.
blocks.zh:
已经广泛探索了深层基因模型,用于无监督域的适应. 其中,基于GAN的方法[6],特别是CycleGAN[22],以及相关的图像到图像的翻译方法[9],在历史上取得了很强的成果. 然而,它们的主要缺点是培训不稳定和缺乏多样性,经常被看到有对抗性的培训目标[6]。 最近,随着传播模式的出现[8,18],新的有趣方法已作为非常有竞争力的替代办法出现. 其中包括流相匹配[12, 1, 20]等方法,这些方法受到持续使流相正常化[2]的启发,并保留从使流相正常化[5]中继承的活字特性,同时能够进行无模拟培训和显著地加快采样. 在这一行中,一些最近的方法超越了标准的高斯假设,允许任意的源和目标分布[20,4,3],从而可以学习在不同图像分布之间直接推向地映射. 最近的相关作品也通过结构化的潜在分解来调查未受监督的域对接与流匹配目标[10]. 或者,有些作品利用神经网络的双射性进行无监督域的适应,最显著的是[7]采用对抗性亏损的流量正常化,并[19]为扩散模型倒置了普通微分方程。 [19]中的工作与我们的方法密切相关,但在三个关键方面有所不同:(一)它为每一种模式培训一个单独的模型,而不是依赖有条件的基因模型;(二)它集成整个ODE解码器,将图像完全映射到高斯噪音上,而我们仅将一部分轨迹整合到在保存图像内容的同时最佳地添加噪音上,这也不同于有条理的片面点名策略,如[13];以及(三)它采用扩散而不是更近的流相匹配范式,已知这种范式可以产生更直的轨迹,更快地集成,并改进图像质量[12].
基于这些优势,我们探索有条件的流量匹配-基于基因的模型,作为无监督域的适应的替代方案,其动机是其稳定的训练、不可逆的双射图绘制以及明确界定的可能性。 虽然本研究考虑的是有限的一组卫星,但这些特性使它们有希望扩展至GPM星座上的额外传感器.

blocks.en: Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) [ 12 , 1 ] is a generative modeling approach sharing many similarities with diffusion, and stemming from continuous normalizing flows [ 2 ] . It is a simulation-free approach, that does not require integrating ordinary differential equations (ODEs) during training, and enables faster sampling than diffusion based approaches. During training (left), the model learns to map both GMI and F18 images to a standard Gaussian distribution using domain-specific labels. During inference (right), domain adaptation is performed in two steps: first, an F18 image is noised by running the forward ODE from t 0 t_{0} to t 1 t_{1} with the associated label conditioning ( 𝐲 i {\mathbf{y}}_{i} in Eq. 8 ). blocks.en: Datasets. The training dataset consists of all GMI and F18 observations acquired in 2018. Following [ 21 , 16 ] only frequencies useful for precipitation estimation are kept. These correspond to 36.6GHz and 89.0GHz for GMI, and 37.0GHz and 91.6GHz for the SSMIS/S instrument. Both vertical and horizontal polarisations are included, resulting in input images with four channels; whose main differences are summarized in Table 1 . To ensure consistency between sensors, polar regions are excluded from the SSMI/S data (latitudes above 70 ∘ 70^{\circ} N or below 70 ∘ 70^{\circ} S), so as to match the spatial coverage of GMI. The test dataset contains all overlaps between the GMI and F18 satellite images from the year 2019, that have more than 50 pixels with rain rates higher than 3mm/h. This corresponds to roughly 18 × 10 6 18\times 10^{6} adapted, collocated pixels from the F18 to the GMI domain.

blocks.en: Evaluation Metrics. To assess the performance of our method, we employ the DRAIN framework [ 21 ] to estimate raining rates from the adapted F18-to-GMI images. Those are then compared with RRs obtained from the original GMI images. To ensure pixels between these images are matched, a KDTree algorithm is applied to find the nearest neighbors within a region of 10km, before calculating distance metrics such as the mean error (ME), mean absolute error (MAE), and the root mean squared error (RMSE). Besides precipitation estimation, we also perform a qualitative assessment of the adapted images. Implementation Details. Experiments are conducted using a class-conditional DiT [ 14 ] , trained for 50 epochs using the Adam optimizer with a learning rate of 1.0 × 10 − 4 1.0\times 10^{-4} and a batch size of 64. The model uses patch embeddings of size 4, 12 attention heads across 12 transformer layers, and a hidden dimension of 384, resulting in a total of 32.91M parameters. During training, input images are randomly cropped to a resolution of 128 × 128 128\times 128 and augmented with random horizontal and vertical flips. In practice, when performing domain adaptation, we set the time variables t 0 t_{0} and t 1 t_{1} from Eq. 8 , to respectively 0.0 and 0.5. For the ODE solver, we use the default Dormand-Prince method from the torchdiffeq library [ 2 ] . Baselines and Comparative Methods. For the baseline, we use the non-adapted F18 images as direct input to our generative model. For the comparative methods, we evaluate against three approaches: (i) stochastic diffusion noising (as in [ 13 ] ), where Eq. 2 is applied with random Gaussian noise to perturb samples at t = 0.5 t=0.5 ; (ii) full ODE noising (as in [ 19 ] ), which is a special case of our formulation with t 1 = 1.0 t_{1}=1.0 in Eq. 8 ; and (iii) CycleGAN (from [ 16 ] ), which also focused on adapting F18 images to the GMI domain.

blocks.en: Table 2 shows the performance of the proposed unsupervised domain adaptation method, when compared to the F18 baseline, and the comparative methods. Overall the proposed method achieves highest performance on moderate and heavy rainfalls. This is valuable because the heavy-tailed rain distribution is the least present in satellite images, meaning the proposed model generalized very well. This is confirmed in Figure 2 , where we compare precipitation estimates on the adapted F18-to-GMI images, with the ground truth GMI, as well as with the comparative methods and the unadapted F18 images. Finally, in Figure 3 , we directly show the radiometer images before and after being adapted. It can be observed that the resolution improves significantly compared to the original F18 images, revealing much finer details. Additionally, our proposed method is less prone to hallucinating details that were not initially present in the original images, unlike competing methods.

blocks.en: In this paper, we presented a novel approach for unsupervised domain adaptation using conditional flow matching. The strength of our method lies in its ability to perform precise, content-aware modifications through invertible and gradual transformations governed by conditional ODEs. Our experiments demonstrate the benefits of this unsupervised domain adaptation approach, highlighting its effectiveness in two-domain scenarios — and showcasing great promise for multiple domains. As future work, we aim to extend this method to handle multiple satellite instruments both within and beyond the GPM-Core constellation, further exploring its potential for large-scale multi-domain adaptation.
blocks.zh: 在本文中,我们提出了一种新颖的方法,即使用有条件的流量匹配来进行不受监督的域调整. 我们方法的优点在于它能够通过由有条件的ODE规范的不可逆和渐进的转换来进行精确的,有内容意识的修改. 我们的实验证明了这种不受监督的领域适应办法的好处,突出了它在两个领域设想中的有效性——并显示出对多个领域的巨大希望。 作为今后的工作,我们力求扩大这一方法,在GPM-Core星座内外处理多颗卫星仪器,进一步探索其大规模多领域适应的潜力。
